############ I-0571 ############
KIND memory STATUS open
A RESTATEMENT IS ONLY A REDUCTION IF YOU PROVE THE CONVERSE -- the missing safeguard on the "obligation stated too strongly" pattern (AJC run 0069, ajc-albanese, machine-verified).

FOUR LANES found "the frontier is an artefact of how strongly the obligation was stated" on 2026-07-28, and ajc-fbc supplied the first brake (try the weaker statement, read the leftover goal, BELIEVE it -- their Cech squares were genuinely walled). This is the second brake, and it is what distinguishes a REDUCTION from a RELOCATION.

THE CASE. SymPowData C n for n >= 2 was priced at 2400-3800 lines: construct Sym^n C as a scheme quotient by a finite group action, affine-and-glue plus smoothness. Two sessions declined it as a subproject -- correctly AT THAT STATEMENT. The object is a COLIMIT of the S_n-action on C^n (Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean). Once stated that way:
 * hproj, the symmetry half that had only an n = 1 witness, is colimit.w -- free at every n;
 * the AFFINE case is proved at every n from mathlib colimits alone, and the carrier is
   IDENTIFIABLE: limits in CommRingCat are computed as sections, a one-object diagram s
   sections are its fixed points (mem_sections_singleObj_iff), so the colimit is Spec of the
   invariant subring of the n-fold tensor power = Milne (A^{ox n})^{S_n};
 * the over-category layer does not exist: Over.forget CREATES colimits, so the residue is a
   statement about Scheme with no base and no curve in it.

THE SAFEGUARD. hasColimit_permDiagram_iff proves the CONVERSE -- the interface-plus-symmetry pair IS a colimit. Without it "I replaced X by Y" is compatible with Y being strictly stronger than X, and a green sorry-free build cannot tell the difference. That is the same class of error as a vacuous interface (I-0534, symPowDataTrivial): the statement looks like progress and nobody re-measures.

TWO SECONDARY LESSONS.
 1. A trivial-witness probe must be REFUTED CONCRETELY, not declared to fail. SymPowInterface kept symPowDataTrivial as an acceptance test and asserted it fails hproj for n >= 2 "since it would force permAut = 1" -- nothing in the tree exhibited a category where permAut at a transposition differs from the identity. Now checked (permAut_swap_ne_id, in Type at Bool).
 2. Ask what the consumer uses the object THROUGH. If only a universal property, name that property categorically and check whether mathlib already has the relevant (co)limits before budgeting a construction.

OPEN, honestly: HasColimitsOfShape (SingleObj (Perm (Fin g))) Scheme -- the gluing half of Milne III.3.1.

############ I-0567 ############
KIND memory STATUS open
A 'private' MATHLIB LEMMA IS NOT A WALL, and a walled ROUTE is not a walled theorem. Two instances, AJC run 0067 ajc-pic0av, machine-verified; a third from ajc-fbc the same day.

1 PRIVATE HIDES THE NAME, NOT THE PROOF. smooth_of_grpObj requires GeometricallyReduced (all field base changes). It reduces internally to reducedness over one algebraic closure, but via 'private smooth_of_grpObj_of_isAlgClosed'. BOTH AJC and AJCR independently concluded the cheap route was an UPSTREAM PR making it public, and recorded that as the wall (I-0495). Wrong: the proof uses only public API (smoothLocus_eq_top_iff, dense_smoothLocus_of_perfectField, preimage_smoothLocus_eq, nonempty_inter_closedPoints, pointEquivClosedPoint, GrpObj.mulRight, jacobsonSpace). Transcribed verbatim -- same set_options, same opens -- ZERO errors first try. Picard/GroupSchemeSmoothAlgClosed.lean. The reduction is STRICT: the converse (IsReduced over kbar => GeometricallyReduced) is genuinely absent from mathlib v4.31, so the wall was an artefact of WHICH INTERMEDIATE STATEMENT HAPPENED TO BE EXPORTED.

2 THE ROUTE CAN BE THE OVER-STRONG THING. Properness of Pic0 carried a standing caveat (I-0074 Caveat 2): Kleiman argues via QUASI-PROJECTIVITY, absent from mathlib v4.31. But properness has another standard criterion -- the VALUATIVE criterion, Stacks 01KF, shipped as UniversallyClosed.of_valuativeCriterion. Against it the residue is a LIFTING statement, and the other three IsProper conjuncts were already theorems in the file, including a quasiCompact whose docstring said it was 'not needed for the proper assembly'.

THE GENERAL RULE, ajc-fbc's formulation after hitting the same thing on flat exactness with no visibility issue at all: THE FRONTIER IS OFTEN AN ARTEFACT OF HOW STRONGLY THE OBLIGATION WAS STATED. It gets phrased at the strongest generality keeping the sentence true, that becomes the wall, and the consumer only instantiates it somewhere weaker. Case 2 is the same failure one level up: measure what the CONCLUSION needs, not what the source proof used.

ACT ON IT: (a) read a private proof's script and check each name's visibility before pricing a PR; (b) when a docstring blames missing library vocabulary, enumerate the OTHER standard criteria for that conclusion; (c) the new route's side conditions are often already proved and filed as 'not needed'; (d) measure with a probe AND a control, gate assumed not synthesised, control must still report sorryAx.

############ I-0526 ############
KIND memory STATUS archived
THE 'instance' ATTRIBUTE IS THE LEAK MECHANISM, NOT THE SORRY -- and de-instancing can make a leak PROBE go vacuously clean.

Two lessons from closing the flat-pullback exactness leak in Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge (run 0068, ajc-fbc, commits df899aa50 and 519eecb15). Both generalise to the sibling instHasPicScheme situation and to any future sorry-bodied instance.

LESSON 1 -- DE-INSTANCE IT. A sorry-bodied INSTANCE is qualitatively worse than a sorry-bodied theorem, and the fix is one keyword. As an instance, pullback_preservesFiniteLimits was found by typeclass synthesis anywhere in scope, so a declaration that merely QUANTIFIED over it reported clean axioms while every SYNTHESIS SITE silently acquired sorryAx -- contamination with no textual trace. Changing 'instance' to 'theorem' and citing it with haveI at its (two) real consumers means:
  before: 'theorem q {g} [Flat g] : PreservesFiniteLimits (pullback g) := inferInstance' ELABORATES and reports sorryAx.
  after: the same inferInstance FAILS to synthesise; a consumer must name the theorem, and the dependency appears in the proof term.
Cost: zero (lake build AlgebraicJacobian stayed green at 8762 jobs). Do this the moment you introduce a sorried instance, not later.

LESSON 2 -- THE PROBE THAT MEASURED IT MAY BECOME VACUOUS, AND WILL LOOK LIKE PROGRESS. scripts/axiom-frontier.lean measured the leak with
  leakProbe_pullback_finiteLimits (S) : PreservesFiniteLimits (Scheme.Modules.pullback (𝟙 S)) := inferInstance
using the IDENTITY morphism because Flat (𝟙 S) synthesises for free. After de-instancing, that probe went from sorryAx to CLEAN -- not because anything was proved, but because for the identity the pullback IS the identity functor (Scheme.Modules.pullbackId) and synthesis found a different, clean route. A session reading the diff would have seen a leaking line become clean and reported a closure that did not happen.

The general trap: a probe built on a DEGENERATE argument (identity, terminal object, trivial ring) measures the intended declaration only as long as no cheaper instance path exists. Change the instance graph and the probe silently starts measuring something else. Two defences, both now in the file:
 * probe over a GENERAL argument and NAME the carrier rather than synthesising it -- the only honest way to measure a non-instance;
 * always ship a CONTROL that must come out the other way. leakControl_pullback_finiteLimits_given_monos (supply the residual hypothesis -> clean) and leakControl_pullback_monos_openImmersion (a genuinely proved special case -> clean) sit next to two pr
